config.title: Design Permission System

intro.title: Design Permission System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple permission system to control access to different features in an Angular application. You will learn how to use Angular's structural directives, such as *ngIf, to conditionally show or hide UI elements based on user roles. The core programming concept involves managing application state with TypeScript to define roles and permissions. By the end, you will have a functional system that displays content only to authorized users, using Angular components and TypeScript interfaces.
intro.usecase: Permission systems are fundamental in enterprise applications where different user roles need access to specific features. In Angular applications, you'll implement permission-based UI controls in admin dashboards to show/hide management panels, in e-commerce platforms to restrict product editing capabilities, and in SaaS applications to customize user menus based on subscription tiers. As a developer, you'll use permission directives to conditionally render navigation items, hide sensitive form fields, and disable action buttons based on user roles. This pattern ensures secure, personalized user experiences while maintaining clean, maintainable code structure.

objectives: Construct a permission service to manage user roles and access levels
Implement role-based guards to control route navigation
Configure directive selectors to conditionally render UI elements
Apply permission checks within component templates using structural directives
Initialize and update permission state across multiple components
Integrate permission validation with Angular's dependency injection system
Manipulate DOM elements based on dynamic permission evaluations

steps.title: Set up component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template to the component with a container div, header, and main content area. Inside the container, create a header with an h1 element containing 'Permission System' and a main content area with a div.
steps.hint: Add the template property to the @Component decorator with backticks for multi-line HTML. Use <div>, <header>, <h1>, and <main> elements.

steps.title: Display permissions list with ngFor
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an unordered list (<ul>) that uses *ngFor to iterate through the permissions array and display each permission's name and description in list items (<li>).
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngFor structural directive to loop through the permissions array. Each list item should display the permission's name and description properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Displaying items with *ngFor
  • {{ item.name }} - {{ item.description }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain a list that displays all permissions from the permissions array using Angular's *ngFor directive.
successCriteria: The template contains a <ul> element with *ngFor="let permission of permissions" and displays each permission's name and description in <li> elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using *ngFor correctly and displaying both the name and description properties for each permission.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the permissions list correctly. Remember to use *ngFor to iterate through the permissions array and show each permission's details.

steps.title: Add permission creation form with two-way binding
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a form with two input fields for permission name and description, using [(ngModel)] to bind them to newPermission properties.
steps.hint: Use <form> with <input> elements for name and description. Remember to import FormsModule in your module for ngModel to work.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: form with two-way binding
<form>
  <input [(ngModel)]="item.name" name="name" placeholder="Enter name">
  <input [(ngModel)]="item.description" name="description" placeholder="Enter description">
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a form with two input fields bound to newPermission properties via ngModel.
successCriteria: Form element with two input fields using [(ngModel)] binding to newPermission.name and newPermission.description.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a form, but check that both input fields use [(ngModel)] binding correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form or two-way binding is missing. Review how to use [(ngModel)] with input fields.

steps.title: Wire form submission and delete buttons to handlers
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a submit button inside the form that calls addPermission() when clicked, and add delete buttons in the permissions list that call removePermission() with the permission id.
steps.hint: Use (click) event binding on buttons. For the delete button, pass the permission's id to removePermission().

steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submit button that adds new permissions, and each permission in the list will have a delete button that removes it.
successCriteria: A submit button with (click)="addPermission()" is added inside the form, and each list item has a delete button with (click)="removePermission(permission.id)".
